text:
jamie.ops: kicking off customer-nova warmup & cutover — private VPC, air-gapped delivery. please use this thread for live notes and blockers. target cutover window: 03/25 02:00-05:00 UTC.

sanjay.eng: on it. do we have final CIDR and allowed egress list from customer?

maria.net: confirmed CIDR 10.12.0.0/16. customer will open outbound to our registry IPs on 443 and to S3 endpoint 198.51.100.34:443. no inbound from internet.

lee-infra: noted. for airgap we need to mirror images to the bastion + verify sha256. I'll run rsync -> scp to the USB seeder if they insist on physical media.

nina-sre: quick health goals for warmup: GPU driver + nv peer mem verified, kernel 5.15+, nvidia-smi shows all GPUs, kubelet registering nodes within 3 mins.

jamie.ops: checklist (short):
- network handshake + firewall rules confirmed by customer
- mirror registry + image verification
- seed node bootstrapped + kubeadm join tokens prepared
- GPU drivers + CUDA bundle preloaded
- service account certs + KMS config (customer KMS)
- smoke infer job (small model) and nvlink throughput test
- cutover runbook read-through

lee-infra: copying command I used for registry mirror in our last airgap:```bash
# on staging mirror host
./mirror-tool pull redwood/runtime:2026-03-10 && ./mirror-tool save ./bundle.tar && sha256sum bundle.tar
# transfer bundle to bastion with scp
scp bundle.tar bastion:/srv/airgap/ && ssh bastion 'sudo ctr images import /srv/airgap/bundle.tar'```

maria.net: firewall snippet customer needs to add:```
# allow egress to our registry + s3
iptables -A OUTPUT -d 203.0.113.17 -p tcp --dport 443 -j ACCEPT
iptables -A OUTPUT -d 198.51.100.34 -p tcp --dport 443 -j ACCEPT
# drop other internet outbound if air-gapped
iptables -A OUTPUT -o eth0 -j DROP
```

sanjay.eng: driver install note: use the signed bundle per customer policy, do not use auto-fetch. command sequence on node:```bash
sudo dpkg -i /opt/cuda/drivers/*.deb
sudo systemctl restart nvidia-persistenced
# verify
nvidia-smi -L && nvidia-smi topo -p2p
```

nina-sre: nvlink check: run this quick test after join:```bash
python - <<'PY'
import torch
print(torch.cuda.device_count())
print(torch.cuda.get_device_name(0))
PY
# we also run a 1GB allreduce to measure throughput -> target > 80 GB/s for A100 NVLink pair
```

ops-bot: deploy-job/airgap-mirror-198 triggered by lee-infra — status: pulling images (45%).

jamie.ops: region constraint note: customer cluster is in eu-west-3 colo rack. inventory there has only 4x A100 nodes and 8x T4 nodes. if we need sustained heavy infer, we should propose reserved capacity + autoscale burst in our hosted pool. cost rough: 4 A100 reserved ~= $38k/month, adding burst in hosted reduces commit to 2 A100 but adds egress/usage cost. thoughts?

sanjay.eng: recommend reserve 2 A100, test qps with warmup, fallback to T4 with quantized models for non-peak. that keeps monthly commit ~ $20k and burst on demand covers spikes.

maria.net: customer accepted KMS integration but wants logs to be forwarded to their SIEM over TLS on 10.12.2.45:6514. will add firewall rule.

lee-infra: blocker: bastion's MTU defaults to 1500; their internal fabric is 9000. need to set MTU 9000 on bonded0 on bastion and all nodes to avoid fragmentation for large image transfers.

jamie.ops: good catch. add to preflight: set MTU, validate with iperf3.

nina-sre: preflight run order I'm going to execute 1) seed node attest + apply kubeadm, 2) driver + nv driver load, 3) kubelet join, 4) GPU labeling + taints, 5) deploy runtime and run smoke infer. I'll log results to the ticket.

ops-bot: deploy-job/airgap-mirror-198 status: completed successfully. bundle sha256: 3b2f8a1d...

sanjay.eng: mirror complete — beginning node bootstrap now. sharing join token in secure ticket.

lee-infra: kubeadm join worked on first try, nodes Registered: 6 total (4 A100, 2 T4). kube-system pods are initializing.

nina-sre: ran GPU smoke: `nvidia-smi -L` ✓, small model infer (distil) 50ms p95 ✓. nvlink test shows expected peer bandwidth. logging attachments in ticket.

maria.net: customer performed network acceptance tests: throughput baseline 9.2 Gbps per node (jumbo frames enabled). no packet loss.

jamie.ops: cutover schedule still on. last step before traffic flip: run canary with 5% of inference traffic to private cluster for 30m. if error rate < 1% proceed.

sanjay.eng: canary deployed. watch dashboard: route /infer to new cluster with header x-cutover:canary.

ops-bot: canary-check running -> 30m started. alerts configured: latency > 500ms or error rate >1%.

lee-infra: minor issue: kube-proxy conntrack table hit 50% under canary load, bumped `conntrack-max` on nodes and rolled kube-proxy daemonset. fixed.

nina-sre: canary 30m done: error rate 0.2%, p95 latency stable. recommends proceed.

maria.net: customer ok to flip. their support will monitor.

jamie.ops: flip in 10. ops team on standby. :shipit: 

ops-bot: cutover-job/198 completed. DNS updated.

lee-infra: post-cutover checks: all pods healthy, GPU utilization ramping as traffic shifts, no OOM. disk IOO steady.

nina-sre: cost note: after flip observed average GPU utilization ~ 35% for first 6 hours. we'll autoscale down A100s to 3 reserved if sustained <40% and rely on burst. open PR for cost adjustment.

jamie.ops: excellent work team. closing runbook and uploading final delivery checklist to the customer ticket. I'll schedule a 1-hour retrospective tomorrow 09:00 UTC.

maria.net: thanks everyone. saved configs: `/opt/airgap/bastion/configs/10.12.0.0-seed.yml`.

sanjay.eng: leaving a quick note for followups: add automated MTU detection to our provisioning script and add conntrack tuning to k8s node profile.

lee-infra: agree. will open infra tickets for both.

nina-sre: adding postmortem template entries: "image transfer validation", "conntrack tuning", "canary thresholds".

jamie.ops: good. thread closed after retrospective. :white_check_mark:
